recipes.name: Spicy Tex-Mex Pizza
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (16 ounce) can spicy fat-free refried beans*
2 cups shredded hearts of romaine lettuce
1 cup shredded pepper Jack or Monterey Jack cheese

steps.text: Adjust oven rack to lowest position, and heat oven to 450 degrees. Mix beans and 1/2 cup salsa in a medium bowl. Place crust on a cookie sheet, then spread the bean mixture over crust. Bake until it's crisp and warm, about 10 minutes.

Remove from oven; top with lettuce, green onions and dollop with the remaining salsa. Drizzle (or, if dressing has an easy-pour top, squirt) dressing over pizza. Top with chips and cheese, then return to oven and bake until the cheese melts, about 2 minutes longer. Cut into 6 slices and serve. Copyright 2006 USA WEEKEND and columnist Pam Anderson. raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Tex-Mex Pizza
raw_recipe.description: Refried beans, salsa, and pepper Jack cheese take the familiar pizza south-of-the-border! Top with green onions and ranch dressing to lessen the heat.

review.reviewBody: Awesome with changes. I use either a premade crust or homemade and precook for a few minutes with a little cheese. I mix the entire can of beans with salsa - enough to make it easy to spread (we use HOT salsa so the pizza is hot). I spread the beans on the all ready hot crust and top the beans with LOTS of sharp cheddar cheese. I cook it in the oven until the cheese is melted and browned. That's it! I top slices with lettuce, onion, salsa, sour cream, black olives, etc. It's the best taco pizza ever.

With an addition of taco seasoning and ground beef this was a hit! Loved the toasted tortilla chips on this, and I toasted the bread with a little cheese first. Excellent - a possible substitution for tacos. It's a giant tostada!

I made the recipe almost exactly but I did add season taco hamburger. easy and delicious. I'll make it again. I also use a think crust so next time I will be sure and not bake for the full initial 10 minutes.
This was great. I added some ground beef with taco seasoning to the pizza. I was able to make two pizzas by using the whole can of refried beans. Will def make again!

I actually used two canisters of reduced fat crescent roll dough that I baked, then cooled. I spread the refried beans first which I did add a little homemade taco seasoning, then homemade salsa and just topped with shredded lettuce, chopped tomatoes and olives and the green onions, then the cheese. I then drizzled homemade ranch-mexican dressing over the top. I did not use the tortilla chips only because I don't keep them on hand. Really quick supper and quite enjoyed by my boys. This is great for a last minute dinner on a busy day.
I used a boxed crust mix and sprinkled taco seasoning on the dough before baking. We love this recipe!

Nice change from regular tacos, I added ground beef to the pizza because we wouldn't eat a taco without meat. It was good. Just watch the pizza crust; even if it's not brown on top, it could be burning on the bottom.
This was excellent. I used homemade crust, but everything was perfect.
I made it for a get together and everyone couldn't stop talking about it and wanted the recipe! I'm sure you could add ground beef if you wanted, or seasoned chicken, but I loved it the way it was
I make this too much!! It's so easy and one of the hubby's favorites. I started adding more ingredients! Yum!
Maybe next time I'll spread out the ranch over the top of the pizza, or substitute the ranch dressing for sour cream
Great, simple recipe. I actually used the pre-made pizza crust which made it even easier!
We loved this but did add taco meat which I think made a huge difference. YUM!
its good. not great. it tastes like a big taco bowl. i even ended up eating it with taco bell hot sauce.
